purpose: Establish the tenant-scoped Service Marketplace lifecycle from request and quote through explicit payer confirmation, evidence, acceptance and non-financial settlement reference.
requiredInvariants: Service requests and every lifecycle receipt are PostgreSQL-authoritative, tenant-scoped and idempotent.
Quotes pin an ACTIVE verified ServiceOffering and use integer money or an explicit manual-quote outcome.
Provider selection, payer assignment and payer confirmation are distinct irreversible receipts.
Only the assigned payer can confirm; assignment or selection never creates an obligation.
Execution, evidence, requester acceptance and settlement reference advance in strict order.
Settlement records an external or future-ledger reference and always declares createsFinancialObligation=false.
No accounting path, registration path, Deal Engine mutation, paid dependency, external access or production activation is introduced.
acceptance: The lifecycle is exactly REQUESTED, QUOTED, PROVIDER_SELECTED, PAYER_ASSIGNED, PAYER_CONFIRMED, EXECUTING, EVIDENCE_SUBMITTED, ACCEPTED and SETTLEMENT_RECORDED.
Multiple immutable provider quotes may exist before exactly one quote is selected.
Same-tenant outsiders and cross-tenant actors cannot read or mutate a request unless they are an eligible quoting provider, selected provider, requester or assigned payer.
Direct row mutation without the matching immutable event, audit row and outbox entry rolls back.
Exact command replay returns the original receipt and conflicting replay is rejected.
Concurrent selection or confirmation commands produce one accepted transition and one stale-version result.
A forced audit or outbox failure rolls back aggregate state and append-only receipts.
The scope guard confirms no registration, accounting or role-eligibility path changed.
